about.text: Queries go straight from this Mac to the database; no query, result or password is sent anywhere else. Passwords are stored on this Mac using the operating system's encryption.
about.title: About OpenAsy Database Client
backup.lead: The backup contains connections, saved queries, query history and trusted SSH fingerprints. Passwords and file access are not included.
conn.clientKey: Choose the client key file (Cancel if it is in the certificate file)
conn.deleteQ: Delete the connection {name}? Its saved password is also removed from the Keychain.
conn.failedHelp: Check the host, port, user and password; enable the SSH tunnel or TLS in the connection settings if required.
conn.keychainNote: Stored in the macOS Keychain; not synced.
conn.name: Connection name
conn.privacy: The connection is made directly from this computer to the database; queries and results do not pass through any other server.
conn.reselect: Choose {name} once more for this app: file access is granted to each app separately.
conn.savePw: Store the password encrypted on this device
conns.emptyDesktop: No connections yet. Use + to add a server connection or open an SQLite file.
conns.title: Connections
data.commitFailed: The changes could not be applied; none were saved: {msg}
data.discardQ.text: There are pending changes. Reloading the data discards them.
data.discardQ.title: Discard changes?
data.hint: Edit a cell with Return or a double-click; ⌥⌘N adds a row, ⌘⌫ deletes. Changes wait until Commit and reach the server in one transaction.
data.inTx: A transaction is open on this connection: the changes run inside it and are not permanent until it is committed.
data.loadedMore: {n} / {total} rows loaded · {page} more as you scroll
data.noPk: This table has no primary key: rows are matched by all columns; if duplicates exist, only one is changed.
data.noPkRowid: This table has no primary key: rows are matched by the system’s hidden row identifier (ctid / rowid).
data.previewLead: {n} statements will run on commit (in one transaction).
demo.queryComment: Orders from the last 30 days, with customer name
export.title: Export
history.empty: Queries you run appear here in order; double-click to open one in a new tab.
history.title: Query History
import.failed: Import failed; no rows were added: {msg}
import.lead: Choose a CSV file; its columns are matched to the table’s columns and rows are inserted in one transaction.
import.title: Import into {table}
inspector.cellHint: Select a cell in the results to see its value here; JSON values open as a tree.
link.noConnection: Connection not found. It may have been deleted or added on another Mac.
plan.empty: The plan (EXPLAIN) of the statement at the cursor appears here as a tree; full table scans are marked in yellow.
prod.text: {name} is marked as production and this query changes data or schema.
prod.title: Change in production
query.empty: Results appear here after a query runs.
query.noConn: Open a database or connect first.
query.readOnly: The connection is read-only; the modifying query was not run.
saved.empty: Queries saved with ⌘D in a query tab appear here and in the sidebar.
saved.name: Query name
saved.title: Saved Queries
settings.confirmWrites: Ask before modifying queries on connections labeled Production
settings.keychainNote: Passwords are stored in the macOS Keychain on this Mac only; they are not included in backups or iCloud.
sidebar.label: Connections and schema
ssh.badKey: Could not read the SSH key: {msg}
ssh.changed: The SSH host key has changed; not connected. Expected {a}, got {b}. If the change is intended, remove the old fingerprint in Settings › Connections.
ssh.trustLead: Connecting to {host} for the first time. Compare the fingerprint with the value from the server’s administrator; trust it only if it matches. It is checked from then on.
ssh.unknown: The SSH host fingerprint is not trusted yet: {f}
ssh.unsupportedKey: This SSH key type is not supported: {k}. Use an Ed25519, RSA or ECDSA (PEM) key.
structure.note: Changes are not applied immediately; open the SQL preview from the bar below.
structure.pick: Select a column, index or foreign key to edit it.
sync.done: Statements applied: {n}. The schema was reloaded.
sync.failed: {done} of {total} statements were applied, then an error occurred:
sync.leadMac: The source is the desired state; the target is this window’s connection and is the side that changes. The source can be another connection or another schema on the same connection. Differences are listed with a risk label; a script is built from the selected ones and applied after a preview.
sync.mysqlNote: In MySQL, schema changes cannot be rolled back in a transaction; a backup before applying is recommended.
sync.reviewLead: Script to apply ({n} statements). It can be saved or tried in a query tab first.
sync.title: Schema Sync
tab.closeDirty.text: The tab {name} has unsaved or uncommitted changes.
tab.closeDirty.title: Close tab?
tabs.emptyText: Open a table from the sidebar or start a new query tab.
te.name: Table name
tools.title: Tools
tx.help: Transaction: begin, commit or roll back. While a transaction is open, changes are not permanent until committed.
users.err: Could not read or change user information: {msg}
users.name: Name
users.pick: Select an account on the left.
users.sqlite: SQLite has no users or privileges; access is governed by the file itself.
users.title: Users and Privileges
welcome.dropMac: Drop a .sqlite or .db file on this window or on the Dock icon. Queries go straight to the database.
welcome.f1: SQL editor: autocomplete, multiple tabs, export results as CSV and JSON
welcome.f2mac: Filter and edit table data in place; structure changes are applied with an SQL preview.
welcome.f3: Differences between two schemas are shown side by side; selected changes are applied
welcome.leadMac: Connect to PostgreSQL, Redshift, MySQL and MariaDB servers, or open SQLite files directly. Connections go straight from this Mac to the database.
welcome.title: Databases, queries and models
